synthesis.one_paragraph_diagnosis: The architecture feels unclear because the repository has no declared or enforced package layering, and the code has grown by "extract-and-re-export" rather than by concept. Measured over argus_skill/: 1,586 cross-package import statements, 67% of them inside function bodies (1,068 lazy vs 518 module-level); 33-35 mutual package pairs, 27 of which exist only because one direction is hidden in a function body; 181 cross-package imports of `_private` modules or names across 53 pairs. The only executable boundary rule (tests/test_architecture_invariants.py:261-317, 27 tests) guards one seam: framework must not import a named vertical. Everything else is a mesh: `core` (fan-in 796) imports agent_cli, provider_integrations, life and manager at module level; `daemon` imports `apps._runtime`; `life` imports `apps` and `webapi` privates; `manager` imports `apps`; `apps` imports `webapi`. On top of this, six of the largest packages have 0-byte `__init__.py` (core, skills, apps, adapters, daemon, engineer) and their names no longer match their contents (core is 78% not a kernel; skills is ~80% not Skills; apps holds the mission runtime; webapi is 29/31 modules non-HTTP; tools holds a 6.3k-LOC job runtime). The product's spine (LifeWorker -> LifeSupervisor -> _SkillLoopRunner -> SkillLoop -> SupervisedEngineer) is spread over daemon/, life/, apps/, the package root and skills/, sliced by a "line-count target" into mixins that re-export private names. The vocabulary is not fixed: the per-project state directory has 12 identifier names, `project_root` (1,910 uses) points at two different directories, `task`/`mission`/`skill`/`session`/`domain`/`plugin`/`contract`/`handoff` each carry 3-12 meanings, and five modules each claim to be the "canonical"/"sole"/"authoritative" truth for overlapping facts, which is why the same 22 filenames appear both at ~/.argus-skill and inside projects/*. Finally, the written architecture is stale or absent (docs cite modules that no longer exist, README maps 1 of 17 top-level directories, package docstrings describe the pre-daemon "SkillLoop"/"ArgusBot" era), so a newcomer's mental model is fed by names and docs that lie.

root_causes.title: No declared or enforced package layering; the de-facto dependency graph is a mesh held together by function-body imports
root_causes.explanation: Nothing in code, docs or tests states which packages may depend on which. The single executable rule (no framework package imports a named vertical) is satisfied, while every other direction is violated, including the fan-in root `core` importing transports, provider integrations, life and manager at module level. Because 67% of cross-package imports sit inside function bodies, the cycles never fail at import time and are invisible to module-level tooling, so they accumulated: 33-35 mutual pairs, 27 of them lazy-only in at least one direction. This is the structural cause behind 'is apps above daemon or below it?', 'why does importing core.paths load the engineer?', and why nobody can name a leaf package.
evidence: AST measurement (this synthesis): 518 module-level vs 1,068 function-body cross-package import statements in argus_skill/ (67% lazy); 33 mutual pairs, 27 with at least one direction function-body-only; 181 cross-package imports of `_private` modules/names across 53 pairs

root_causes.title: The mission runtime (the product's spine) has no home: it is spread over five packages plus the package root, sliced by line-count rather than concept, and its 'private' names are the real cross-package API
root_causes.explanation: The execution chain LifeWorker -> LifeSupervisor -> _SkillLoopRunner -> SkillLoop -> SupervisedEngineer is linear, but each hop lives in a different package (daemon, life/supervisor, apps, package root + skills/loop_*, engineer). Decomposition was done by 'maintainability line-count target' into mixins and `_runtime_*.py` files that re-export underscore names 'so external imports are unaffected'. The result: the same supervisor is assembled by hand at several sites, the same method is defined in three mixins, and underscore-private modules are imported by other packages and by a third of the test suite. Readers cannot find 'the loop' because there are nine loop-like things with colliding names.

root_causes.explanation: A newcomer's model is fed by docs and docstrings that describe removed modules or an earlier product, by a README that maps 1 of 17 top-level directories, and by a tree where a 39k-LOC companion, a LaTeX paper, a 2 MB generated audit dump, a 2,432-line operator handoff journal and 24 MB of committed build output sit beside the runtime. verify:refute:rc1.corrected_summary: Measured over argus_skill/ (687 modules): 1,594 cross-package import statements, 1,071 (67.2%) inside function bodies versus 32.8% for intra-package and 5.7% for stdlib/third-party imports, so the function-body style is specific to framework cross-package seams (life 79%, apps 81%, manager 81%, core 80%; 1,007 of 1,071 outside verticals). 35 mutual package pairs exist, 28 with one direction lazy-only; 181 private-name imports across 53 pairs; core has fan-in 798 and imports 8 other packages (agent_cli, provider_integrations and life at module level at knobs.py:21, backend_readiness.py:12-13, usage.py:22, operator_messages.py:8, mission_view/_reduce_mission.py:19). No module-level import cycle crosses a package (all 23 module-level SCCs are intra-package), which is why nothing ever failed at import time; but module-level edges alone already make 16 packages one package-level SCC, so the mesh is not merely 'held together' by lazy imports. Only 10 of the 1,071 lazy imports are individually necessary cycle-breakers and only 94 carry a reason comment; hoisting all of them would put 607 inside a 197-module cycle. A real load-bearing reason exists for about 27% of lazily imported names: tests monkeypatch them on their defining module (387 names; 19 tests patch daemon.life_worker.LifeSupervisor alone), documented at daemon/_life_worker_boot.py:6-10 and apps/_runtime_construction.py:651-657. Layering intent is partially written in package docstrings (life 'layer on top', webapi 'thin layer over daemon pub/sub', apps/_runtime naming daemon/team/manager as consumers, proof_ledger as a tested leaf) and in PRINCIPLES.md:29-38, but no document or test states an order among core/life/daemon/apps/manager/webapi/tools; the 8 import-structure tests suite-wide (3 in tests/test_architecture_invariants.py:261-317) all concern verticals, proof_ledger or the doctor. argus_skill/__init__.py:18's eager SkillLoop import (present since the first public commit, no external consumer found) makes `import argus_skill.core.paths` load 71 modules across 8 packages including engineer, reviewer and life.memory (not verticals/daemon/apps/webapi), and forces the stdlib-only argus_doctor.py console script to sit at the repo root.
verify:refute:rc1.strongest_counterargument: The '67% lazy' headline conflates three different things and so overstates how much a layering rule would fix. First, only 10 of 1,071 lazy imports are needed to avoid a module-level cycle today, and module-level imports alone already make 16 packages mutually reachable, so lazy imports are not what 'holds the mesh together' and hoisting or banning them would not by itself reveal or remove the coupling. Second, roughly a quarter of the lazily imported names (387 of 1,430) are deliberate test seams: the suite patches them on their defining module (e.g. 19 tests patch argus_skill.daemon.life_worker.LifeSupervisor, 5 patch apps._runtime.build_life_runner), and two docstrings say so explicitly; these lazies are load-bearing and any mechanical hoist would break tests, so the figure partly measures a testing convention rather than hidden layering violations. Third, several of the headline 'violations' are misfiled leaf modules rather than inverted layers: core's module-level imports of agent_cli/runner_backend.py and life/mission_outcome.py target stdlib-only modules with zero argus imports, and daemon/team/manager importing apps._runtime is exactly the consumer list its own docstring declares. Combined with the fact that partial direction statements do exist (life, webapi, manager, apps/_runtime, proof_ledger docstrings; PRINCIPLES.md Core/Vertical rule) and that proof_ledger is a declared, tested leaf, one could argue the real defect is narrower: three or four misplaced modules, an eager root __init__, and a missing written order — not a pervasive mesh that requires re-layering the whole tree.

Executable import rules exist in 4 test files (tests/test_architecture_invariants.py:261,280,300 - 27 tests, all passing; tests/core/test_vertical_contract.py:356; tests/life/test_result_shortfall_iteration.py:221; tests/proof_ledger/test_proof_ledger_kernel.py:904,931), but all guard either the framework-vs-vertical seam or proof_ledger's isolation; none constrains core/life/daemon/apps/manager/webapi relative to each other, and docs/architecture-simplification-plan.md:37-45 states intent only for core-vs-vertical. 186 of 650 test files import 3+ argus_skill units; tests/daemon/test_life_worker.py imports 6 (apps, core, daemon, life, manager, skills).
verify:remeasure:rc1.strongest_counterargument: The numbers are real, but the framing 'mesh held together by function-body imports' and 'no leaf, no top' overstates the disorder in three ways. First, core is 96% a sink: 789-798 inbound vs 33-35 outbound statements, and only 7 of those outbound are module-level, concentrated in 5 files - a small, mechanically fixable set (move SUPPORTED_BACKENDS/normalize_runner_backend down into core, invert the JsonlEventSink and mission_outcome dependencies, move `__version__`), after which core would be a genuine kernel without any restructuring. Second, several of the lazy imports are documented, deliberate dependency-management choices rather than accidents (daemon/_life_worker_boot.py:238-239: 'keeps daemon.life_worker free of CLI-only deps until needed'), and 6 of the 33 cycles are module-level both ways yet cause no import failure, so function-body imports are not what 'holds the cycles together' - Python tolerates package-level mutual imports between distinct modules regardless. Third, there ARE enforced leaves the diagnosis omits: proof_ledger has an executable 'imports nothing from argus_skill' test and fan-out 0, wiki has fan-out 3 and domains 2, and five import-rule tests exist across four files rather than 'the only' rule in one. The strongest version of the objection is that the real problem is the absence of a written layering statement (which is cheap to add as one invariant test over the directional-count table already computed here), not the size of the mesh, and that the same evidence supports 'a few dozen misplaced edges around a mostly-layered graph' as well as it supports 'no layering at all'.

Finally, some cited numbers are soft: two different core groupings both land on exactly 1,547 LOC, the 4,545-LOC 12-file grouping and the manager 11% slice cannot be uniquely reconstructed, and the webapi '80% not web' figure ignores routes/ where all 15 modules are genuine FastAPI code.

verify:refute:rc3.corrected_summary: The linear chain LifeWorker._rf_main_loop (daemon/_life_worker_run.py:272) -> LifeSupervisor.run/tick (life/supervisor/_core.py:697/:1151) -> _SkillLoopRunner.execute (apps/_runtime_execute.py:412) -> SkillLoop.run (loop.py:270, mixins in skills/loop_*.py) -> SupervisedEngineer.run (engineer/runner.py:103) really does cross five packages plus the package root, and nothing in docs/ (0 architecture docs mention any of these classes; the simplification plan does not either), the 0-byte daemon/apps/engineer/skills __init__.py files, or tests/test_architecture_invariants.py names it as a unit. Its cross-package surface is genuinely underscore-named: life/supervisor/__init__.py declares 30 names of which 24 are private, apps/_runtime.py declares 23 of which 19 are private, and 180 private cross-package imports exist in production (147 lazy, 33 module-level; 57 of them are the verticals._base seam that belongs to root cause #6; only 21 hit an __all__-declared name). Stale docstrings are real: 'daemon.mission_executor.MissionExecutor' (3 files) and 'JsonlCommandBus' do not exist, loop.py still describes the ArgusBot era, and daemon/life_worker.py:31-46 re-exports stdlib modules as monkeypatch seams. God-file sizes (3,164/2,432/2,230/2,457/1,549) and the three lazy-held cycles (daemon<->apps 3+16, apps<->manager 12+6, manager<->life 13+22) are exact. However the 'duplication' half of the argument does not survive: _emit_planner_verdict has ONE 113-LOC implementation plus two raise-NotImplementedError host stubs (standard mixin idiom, 5 such stubs in the package); the 'quadruplicated' front door is a five-layer composition stack around a single model classifier (life/router.classify_front_door <- manager/_front_door_ops <- apps/_self_reply (calls manager.route) <- manager/front_door.manager_triage (calls chat_reply_if_conversational) <- webapi/manager_bridge+manager_dispatch (delegate to _front_door_classify)), with two real orchestrators (foreground vs web), the identically-named manager_*_handoff wrappers, and a dispatch.py name collision as the actual defects; the two LifeSupervisorConfig builders (apps vs daemon) have different signatures, share sub-helpers, and are documented as the intended cockpit-vs-daemon duality in daemon/life_worker.py:1-8; and the 13 'line-count target' modules each carry a phase/concern docstring (runner construction, execute lifecycle, stage transition, admission, boot, identity, run, runtime context, round config), so the slicing was by lifecycle phase with line-count as the stated trigger, and no test or lint enforces any target. Number corrections: LifeSupervisor has 10 direct mixins, 17 classes in its MRO, and 207 methods (229 counting properties and dunders), not 248; test_life_worker.py touches 15 modules by import (23 with monkeypatch strings), not 29; 269 (not 233) test files import something private and 184 (not 186) import 3+ subpackages; the daemon/config.py private import cited as the lead example carries an explicit cycle-break comment. Production consumers of apps/_runtime's private re-exports are 4 names in 2 packages (daemon, team); the rest of that surface exists for 11 test files.
verify:refute:rc3.strongest_counterargument: The runtime is not homeless so much as un-mapped: every hop's module docstring already names its neighbours and its layering rule (life/__init__.py 'Public surface (intentionally small)'; manager/__init__.py 'Mission execution remains with the existing LifeSupervisor engine'; apps/_runtime.py 'shared by the daemon, teammate runner, and Manager front-door ... independent of the Ink/Web presentation layer'; daemon/life_worker.py 'cockpit and daemon both build the same LifeSupervisor'), the module-level import graph shows a coherent de-facto direction (life at the bottom, apps/manager/daemon above, webapi on top; broken at module level only by life/telegram_bot.py:29 and life/chat/router.py:35-36), and the split modules are by lifecycle phase, not arbitrary line slices. The concrete 'duplicates' the diagnosis points to are mostly not duplicates (one _emit_planner_verdict implementation, one front-door classifier composed through five layers, two documented supervisor-config builders for two hosts), so the 'delete the copies' remedy the title implies has little to delete. The genuinely measurable defects are declarative: 24/30 and 19/23 underscore names in __all__, 0-byte __init__.py in four of the five spine packages, three stale docstrings, name collisions (dispatch.py, manager_*_handoff), and 22 lazy life->manager plus 11 life->daemon imports that reverse the otherwise visible direction. Those are fixable by renaming exported names, writing package docstrings, and adding an executable 'no framework package imports another package's _module' invariant, without moving a single class; and the private-import traffic that would resist such a rule is dominated by tests (269 files) and by the verticals._base seam (63/180), which are root cause #6 and a test-hygiene issue rather than evidence that the runtime lacks a home.

verify:remeasure:rc3.corrected_summary: The mission-execution chain is real and strictly linear, but each hop sits in a different package: daemon/_life_worker_run.py:272 -> life/supervisor/_core.py:697/1151 -> life/supervisor/_mission_execution_runtime.py:840 -> apps/_runtime_execute.py:412/818/1085 -> loop.py:270 (root, assembled from 4 mixins in skills/loop_*.py) -> engineer/runner.py:103. Thirteen modules (6 apps/_runtime*, 6 daemon/*life_worker*, engineer/round_config.py) declare they were split purely to meet a 'maintainability line-count target' and re-export underscore names so 'external imports are unaffected'; apps/_runtime.py's __all__ is 19/23 private and tools/subagent/__init__.py's is 69/91 private. LifeSupervisor is composed from 10 direct mixins (17 classes in the MRO) with ~207-212 methods (not 248), _planning_context.py is one 2,432-LOC mixin with 66 methods, and _emit_planner_verdict is defined three times in that one MRO. LifeSupervisor is constructed by hand at 3 production sites with two identically-named _build_supervisor_config builders in apps and daemon. Production code has exactly 181 private cross-package import statements across 53 package pairs, and daemon<->apps, apps<->manager, manager<->life are all genuine import cycles (34 mutual pairs overall). In the 650-file test suite, 172 files import an underscore module path and 269 import an underscore module or name (the diagnosis's 233 lies between these two definitions); 184 files import 3+ subpackages. The Manager front door exists in four places (manager/front_door.py 1,526 LOC; webapi/manager_*.py 3,806 LOC; apps/_self_reply.py 1,133 LOC; life/router.py:367 imported back by manager/_front_door_ops.py:50). Two supervisor docstrings reference components that do not exist (daemon.mission_executor.MissionExecutor, JsonlCommandBus). God-file line counts are exact as stated.
verify:remeasure:rc3.strongest_counterargument: The dispersal is the residue of a deliberate, documented decomposition, not accidental drift: every `_runtime_*.py` / `_life_worker_*.py` split says why it exists and re-exports every name, so nothing broke and every hop in the chain has exactly one production caller (loop.py is imported from only two places; LifeSupervisor is built at only three). Read that way the runtime does have a home — life/supervisor for policy and apps/_runtime for driving — and the real defect is narrower than 'no home': underscore-prefixed modules are being used as the stable API (181 cross-package statements, 172-269 test files), the split was by size rather than concept, and a few names collide. Those are naming/visibility problems fixable by mechanical rename-plus-shim batches, not evidence that the architecture lacks a spine. The 'nine loops' and '248 methods' figures also overstate the mess (6 Loop classes, ~207-212 methods), and Python test suites reaching into private modules is a common convention rather than a structural failure.

verify:refute:rc4.corrected_summary: Root cause #4 is real but narrower than stated. Every number reproduces (identifier counts exact; task 1,897/1,021 and mission 1,264/687 within 5%; ids exact; 22 dual-level filenames exact; 19 global maintenance cards; 108 EventType members with life.* 49 / round.* 11). The load-bearing defect is one ambiguous property: `MemoryBundle.root` returns the global ~/.argus-skill root (life/memory.py:3004) while `LifeMemory.root` is the project dir; the daemon's normal path builds a MemoryBundle (daemon/_life_worker_boot.py:215-223) and life/supervisor uses `self.memory.root` 84 times and `self.memory.project_root` 0 times, which directly produces live global-root copies of letters.json, RESEARCH_PLAN.md, stage-certificates.json, runtime-failure-circuit.lock and campaign-control (mtimes 2026-09-13); four shims (_life_dir_for, _project_state_root, _memory_project_root, _lifecycle_root) and a 20-line bug-postmortem comment (manager/front_door.py:268-285) exist because of it, and no test guards it. Docstring staleness (matcher/ArgusBot/argus.manager/_VENDORED.md) is fully confirmed. The 'N names for one concept' bullets are inflated: of the 12 state-dir identifiers, state_dir (44/128 in trial/), runtime_root (22/99 = global root or sandbox) and vertical_state_root (defaults to workdir, documented as a distinct root) are wholly or partly different concepts; of the 22 dual-level files ~7 are two-scope by design (identity.md, events.jsonl, skills/, operator_context.*, maintenance/); of 5 'mission' senses 4 are facets of one mission; of 5 role-name sites 3 differ in content deliberately, though 6 identical copies of the 4-tuple do exist. 'Not fixed in code' is false at three seams: tests/test_architecture_invariants.py pins the four prelude root names keyword-only at every vertical call site and provider, pins RoleName to the prompt catalog, and pins the gate vocabulary. CORE_CONCEPTS.md fixes life_dir, defines project root = workdir, and documents the MemoryBundle.root=global caveat; Manager, SessionMeta, core/paths.session_state_root and verticals/_base.py each state the workdir/state-root distinction in code. docs/architecture-simplification-plan.md does not mention vocabulary at all.
verify:refute:rc4.strongest_counterargument: The distinctions this root cause says are missing are in fact written down where the code crosses a boundary — the Manager class docstring, SessionMeta's inline comment, core/paths.session_state_root ('never its execution workdir'), the verticals/_base.py prelude docstring, and two executable invariants that pin the four root names and the four role names — and CORE_CONCEPTS.md already declares life_dir canonical and documents the MemoryBundle.root caveat. What remains is not an unfixed vocabulary but a single hazardous accessor (`MemoryBundle.root`, 88 uses, 84 of them in the supervisor with zero uses of the unambiguous `project_root` sibling) plus ~6 copy-pasted role tuples; that is a two-batch mechanical fix (delete/rename one property behind a shim, import one ROLES constant), and it is the mechanism behind almost all of the on-disk duplication symptom. The rest of the 'collision' inventory (task, mission, session, contract, handoff) is largely ordinary reuse of common English words in different layers with distinct types, and the event-name prefixes are a persisted wire format that no PRINCIPLES-compliant proposal could rename without a migration mechanism — so ranking 'vocabulary' as a top-4 architectural root cause overstates a defect that is mostly one property and one tuple.

verify:remeasure:rc4.root_cause_title: The domain vocabulary is not fixed in code: one concept has many names and one name has many concepts, and the documented hierarchy (Operator -> Project -> Mission -> Role) is not the dominant vocabulary

verify:refute:rc5.corrected_summary: Durable-state ownership in Argus is decentralised rather than absent. core/paths.py (141 LOC, 15 public functions) resolves 12 host-root paths and scopes itself to that by docstring; the other ~55 distinct filenames are each declared exactly once by their owning module (57 constants, one duplicate: events.jsonl declared in life/event_log.py and two webapi modules), and docs/CORE_CONCEPTS.md:104-114 already carries a 7-row concept-to-storage table. The six 'authority' docstrings do not conflict: two describe the same events.jsonl consistently, cost_control.py explicitly defers to usage.jsonl and only reads it, and HEAD.json / DONE are distinct facts. complete_project has exactly one caller; the five disable_continuous_config sites are operator pause/stop/drain writes that preserve the objective, not DONE writes. Of the seven 'objective' fields, three hold the project objective as text (session.json first-write, continuous.json, goal_contract.json), two are sha256 fingerprints derived from continuous.json with the direction stated in code, and two are per-mission instructions. What does hold: 19 atomic-write definitions of which ~12 are near-identical tmp+os.replace variants (5 differ materially: precommit/dir-fsync/ENOSPC reserve for continuous.json, Windows retry, path confinement, force flag); 31 files lock by hand while core/file_lock.py offers only one mode (exclusive, bounded wait) so ~10 try-lock, 1 shared-lock and 2 msvcrt sites cannot use it as-is; the mission-view projection is updated from inside JsonlEventSink._append with no stated rationale and re-reduced by a ~380-LOC TS reducer with no shared parity fixture; _snapshot.py and missionView.ts accept 'in_progress'/'claimed' that backlog rows never carry; eventCatalog.ts names are hand-synced by a regex test; Backlog.update silently coerces unknown statuses to 'pending'; two activity-file lists (session.py, project_gc.py) disagree in membership; 57 stale daemon.health.json sidecars persist after exit. The real, narrower root cause is: no shared write/lock/tail primitive in core and a UI read model owned by the event appender, not a missing owner of durable truth.
verify:refute:rc5.strongest_counterargument: The evidence bullets inflate three genuine mechanics problems (one atomic-write helper missing, a single-mode lock helper, a projection hooked into the appender plus a second TS reducer) into a claim about 'no owner for durable state' by counting things that are not duplicates: constants declared once per owning module, sha256 fingerprints derived from a stated source, per-mission objectives vs the project objective, status vocabularies for citations and proof nodes, docstrings that defer to each other, and operator pause writes labelled as bypasses of the DONE path. Once those are removed, the durable-state layer looks like a deliberately decentralised design with one documented DONE writer (one caller), one documented event appender, one continuous.json owner (daemon/state.py, with ENOSPC protection because it is the daemon kill-switch), and a docs table plus an existing plan (architecture-simplification-plan.md) already scheduling the remaining-work consolidation. A restructuring that adds a core atomic_write_json + try-lock mode to file_lock.py, moves update_mission_view_event out of _append into a log consumer, and adds a Python/TS reducer golden fixture would address what is actually confirmed here without needing a new 'state owner' package.

verify:remeasure:rc5.corrected_summary: Verified: six modules carry self-declared 'canonical/sole/authoritative/one transaction' docstrings (life/memory.py:5, life/event_log.py:6-7, core/usage.py:3, core/cost_control.py:3, manager/control_state.py:3-4, core/project_api.py:1); project_api.py:6-11 itself enumerates four 'done' facts but complete_project writes only lifecycle.json, while continuous.json's done_reason is set by disable_continuous_config from 5 call sites in 4 files (apps/_life_actions.py:364, life/chat/router.py:590, webapi/manager_dispatch.py:133/988, daemon/state.py:1511) that never pass through project_api. The objective is stored or hashed in 7 places (session.py:59, daemon/state.py:82-89, context_packet.py:333/400, project_contract.py, control_state.py:121, directive.py:97-104, memory.py:878); remaining work in 5 artifacts (CHECKPOINT.md path composed in 6 files, frontier.json, review.next_action, capsule open_hypotheses at role_session.py:152-391, acceptance_check at memory.py:944), already named in docs/architecture-simplification-plan.md:33-35; operator intent in 5 stores plus 20 planner-waiting-contract-*.json singletons on disk. Layout: core/paths.py is 141 LOC / 17 defs (15 public) and names 12-13 files/dirs, versus 34-37 *_FILENAME/*_DIRNAME constants in 21-24 files (83 in 47 if _FILE/_DIR counted), 213 def *_path/_dir/_root helpers outside it, four hand-rolled 'state files' tuples at the cited lines (training_capture.py:868 hard-codes /tenant/home), 26 files (39 sites) calling global_root() directly, and 3 files reading ARGUS_SKILL_HOME independently (5 more set it for children). Runtime projects show ~70-88 distinct project-level filenames. Primitives: exactly 19 atomic_write defs, 32 files using flock/portalocker/LOCK_EX vs 17 importers of the 48-LOC core/file_lock.py, a 64KB reserve-file scheme for continuous.json (state.py:56, 374-435), at least 9 JSONL tail readers, 3 _resolve_global_root copies. Projection: event_log.py:286-292 lazily imports core.mission_view inside the locked append and _dispatch.py:122-124 rewrites mission-view.json per handled event; _snapshot.py:149 merges backlog statuses 'in_progress'/'claimed' that memory.py never writes (0 hits); missionView.ts:754-773 copies the snapshot and replays via a ~380-LOC reducer (~497 with mergeSnapshot); 109 event names are kept in sync across EventType, event_payload_schemas.json and eventCatalog.ts by a regex test at tests/core/test_event_catalog.py:221-236; wording lives in 5 tables. Liveness: 80 projects, daemon.status.json in 3, daemon.health.json in 57, daemon.pid in 3, continuous.json in 38, 7 webapi-*.owner.json, two lock dirs each mixing 's-*' and 12-hex ids; 42 module-level *_STATUSES sets in 22 files; Backlog.update (memory.py:1743-1747) coerces unknown status to 'pending'. Counts that did not reproduce: 46 global_root() files (measured 26), 13 ARGUS_SKILL_HOME readers (measured 3 true readers / 14 mentions), 48/32 FILENAME constants (measured 34-37/21-24), 37 STATUSES (measured 42).
verify:remeasure:rc5.strongest_counterargument: Much of what is counted as 'no owner' is deliberate, documented layering that the team is already converging: core/paths.py is intentionally a minimal root-layout registry (runtime root, projects/, skills/, logs/) and project-level files are declared by their owning module via *_FILENAME constants, which is a legitimate 'owner declares its file' pattern rather than sprawl; the event log really is the single canonical truth and both project_api.py and project_contract.py plus docs/architecture-simplification-plan.md:33-35 show the duplicates are known and slated for deletion behind a MISSION.md rebuild. Several 'copies' of the objective are derived hashes (sha256 in control_state.py:121, directive.py:97) used for staleness detection, not independent truths. The 57-vs-3 daemon.health.json/daemon.status.json split is consistent with an in-progress migration (health.py is the newer writer; daemon_liveness.py still reads the old sidecar) rather than six parallel liveness authorities. The lock sprawl figure (32 files) includes core/file_lock.py itself and modules like core/usage.py and life/event_log.py that predate it, and the 17 importers show adoption is happening; the fix is mechanical consolidation, not evidence of a missing state model. Finally, several headline counts were overstated (global_root 46->26 files, ARGUS_SKILL_HOME 13->3 real readers, FILENAME constants 48->34-37), so the 'everyone resolves paths themselves' framing is softer than the diagnosis implies, even though every structural claim (dual-authored mission view, four 'done' facts with one partial transaction, per-module atomic-write/lock/tail re-implementation) reproduced exactly.

verify:remeasure:rc6.corrected_summary: The only executable domain-blindness rule (tests/test_architecture_invariants.py::test_no_framework_package_imports_a_named_vertical, one of 27 tests) is satisfied by letter while framework code names the research vertical by string: 47 `== / != "research"` comparisons outside verticals/ (manager 15, skills 13, life 7, roles/prompts 4, core 3, reviewer 2, apps 1, loop.py 1), DEFAULT_VERTICAL = "research" defined twice (verticals/_base.py:27, skills/vertical_select.py:133), skills/stage_machine.py:819-820 falling back to the research checklist on any Exception, and a legacy-research stage migration at stage_machine.py:141-190. core/ holds 1,366 LOC of paper/venue/manuscript/evidence policy in five files (venue_review 330 with 75 venue/paper/manuscript lines, repair_freshness 411, manuscript_narrative_runtime 257, evidence_status 194, manuscript_snapshot 174), two of which (evidence_status, repair_freshness) are consumed only by verticals; core/stage_certificate.py:150-153 loads the active vertical via skills.vertical_select and branches on "research" despite core/vertical_contract.py:3 promising never to import a concrete vertical. 23 of 109 catalogued events are wiki.*/skill.*/idea.*/venue.*/research.*. 'research/' is the de-facto artifact directory: 41 quoted 'research/...' literals outside the research vertical, 28 of them inside ten non-research verticals (plus 10 Path("research")/ joins), though research/PIPELINE_STATE.json is now only a legacy fallback (core/pipeline_state.py:13). The contract's value type ChecklistItem (skills/stage_machine.py:21) is imported by 24 files under verticals/+domains/ (23 module-level), and the VERTICALS inventory lives in skills/vertical_select.py:69, so verticals -> skills has 30 imports (24 module-level) while skills -> verticals has 26, all function-local, with 6 cycle comments; verticals/_base.py:89-322 keeps 23 `vertical_*` accessor wrappers 'retained for existing callers' in parallel to core/vertical_contract.py's VerticalContract (157-482, 31 fields). Stage authority ('Manager is the sole writer', apps/_runtime_stage_transition.py:2-3, argus-manager-role.md:8) is asserted only by prose and by advanced_by/reset_by strings: five advance/rollback call sites outside manager/ (life/supervisor/_planning_cycle_enqueue.py:196,205,497; _mission_execution_settlement.py:203; skills/vertical_select.py:1021) label themselves "manager:*", and no test checks writer identity. Ancillary leaks reproduce exactly: research_bridge.py:19 wraps private _query_local_gpus for life/supervisor/_letters.py:345; nvidia-smi in 8 .py files; _default_nanochat_profile 121 LOC in life/; 3 verticals -> manager imports; literary/shared 967 LOC with no stages.py and not in VERTICALS; VERTICALS (24) vs directories (24) differ by digital_circuit_benchmark (aliased at _base.py:29-30) and literary; physics/gates/ holds only __pycache__; verticals is 45,542 LOC with no tests/verticals/ (56 of 74 tests/skills files import argus_skill.verticals).
verify:remeasure:rc6.strongest_counterargument: Much of the 'leak' is the framework legitimately knowing its own default and its own paper-mission feature, not domain policy hidden in core. 13 of the 47 "research" comparisons sit in skills/vertical_select.py and skills/stage_machine.py, whose job is to resolve a vertical and so must name the fallback; 7 more are in manager/domain_author.py which makes the vertical decision; only ~25 are in layers (roles/prompts, life, core, reviewer, loop.py) that should be reading a contract field. The verticals<->skills cycle never fails at runtime (all 26 skills-side imports are already function-local) and its fix is a tiny mechanical move of one frozen dataclass and one tuple into a neutral package, so it is a smell rather than a structural cause. The 1,366 core LOC of venue/manuscript code is 0.6% of the codebase and is gated by the contract's paper-mission fields. The 'research/' artifact directory is a deliberate, already-migrating layout (PIPELINE_STATE moved to .argus/) that live campaigns depend on, so it belongs under keep_as_is rather than root cause. And on stage authority, every non-Manager write site is the supervisor executing a Manager decision and stamps it as such (advanced_by="manager:planner_request"/"manager:auto_completion"), so 'Manager is the sole writer' is true at the decision level even if not at the Python call-site level; the missing piece is one invariant test, not a design flaw.

The `_server_module.py` shim and all 22 F401 re-exports are documented dedup/monkeypatch seams (commit daeb0c247), i.e. the very 'move + re-export shim' pattern the project's constraints prescribe. Launcher drift is real but smaller: of 20 parser flags absent from tui_launcher, 14 are subcommand-scoped and 2 are deliberately cockpit flags, leaving 4 order-sensitive companion flags; 3 launcher flags (--configure-codex, --set-git-global, --accept-house-rules) are genuinely dead; no drift test exists. The TUI spawning `argus-skill --web` is a documented one-command-launch design. Of the 88 `def main(`, 74 are vertical/tool/trial/release scripts. Four UI codebases exist (web React, tui Ink, desktop-tauri iframe shell, argus_skill/cli ANSI renderer — not Rich); parseSSEFrames is byte-identical between web api.ts:539-557 and tui api.ts:247-265; there are at least 4 event renderers, the shared Python one having a single consumer in the daemon stderr sink (apps/_runtime_helpers.py:113).
verify:remeasure:rc7.strongest_counterargument: Much of the counted 'duplication' is layered delegation, not re-implementation: the doctor surfaces collapse to 3 engines that deliberately measure different things (bootstrap environment, per-project daemon checks, host-level report), the 5 status builders serve different audiences with different payload shapes, the 7 update modules and daemon_lifecycle.py are the product of an intentional behavior-preserving split of server.py (documented at _server_module.py:1-8 and daemon_lifecycle.py:3), and the 22 noqa re-exports are mostly test-monkeypatch anchors that a service-layer move would have to preserve anyway. The webapi coupling is real but small and cheap to fix: only 6 modules outside webapi import it, all lazily in function bodies, so relocating roughly a dozen functions into a service package would break the cycle without touching routes. The trial code adds wheel weight but is inert unless enabled, and four UI codebases is partly by design (terminal, browser, desktop shell are distinct delivery targets). Finally, several headline numbers in the original bullet were inflated or imprecise (doctor '5x' vs 3 engines, spawn '9 functions' incl. _core.py which defines none, '8 undeclared flags' vs 3, 'Rich' CLI that uses no Rich), which suggests the sprawl is somewhat overstated even though its direction is correct.

Committed artefacts: frontend/web/dist 186 files / 24 MB touched by 405 of 1,669 commits with only 1 of 18 index-*.js and 9 of 82 .js reachable from index.html, force-included into the wheel at pyproject.toml:142-145 — but .gitignore:11-13 documents the tracking as intentional and server.py:696-698 prefers the same checkout's dist (not a sibling's); two npm logs tracked; tui bundle 774 KB; pyproject/.gitignore exclude four paths with 0 commits in all history; desktop/ holds only an untracked .pyc. The 2,432-line / 52-section / 57-commit handoff journal is the sole record of at least two 2026-09 incidents (copilot prompt-delivery break, strong-accept target), alongside a second 368-line handoff and two dated note files. Tests: 650 files, 201 (42,024 LOC) at tests/ root, 7 argus_skill subpackages without a mirror dir (verticals 43,934 LOC), 56 of 73 tests/skills files test verticals, 14 of 25 test dirs lack __init__.py, 5 milestone-named files, and the two boundary-rule tests live in different dirs.
verify:refute:rc8.strongest_counterargument: Much of the "stale or misleading" evidence comes from documents that already tell the reader not to trust them: CURRENT_ROLE_PROMPTS.md marks itself 已过期, system-audit.md says every number was "measured on the tree at the time of writing", CORE_CONCEPTS.md pins itself to a commit and says references keep their baseline revision, RESEARCH_AGENCY TODO calls itself a backlog "not the current running contract", and ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT.md labels itself heuristic review candidates. Several numeric contrasts are overstated or wrong: "5277 scanned vs 988 tracked" compares three worktree copies of the whole repo with the argus_skill/ subtree alone (whole-repo tracked was 2,056); the README results section last changed 2026-08-25, not 2026-09-10; the v0.1.5/0.1.6 mismatch is a 2-day release lag; technical_report's "dependency" on argus_skill is a string label; desktop/'s .pyc is untracked; and dist tracking plus server.py's source-first lookup are documented deliberate choices (.gitignore:11-13, server.py:691-695), while research/ is the coded default output of a shipped tool and FLYWHEEL's own README states its companion status. Under this reading the true defect narrows to (a) four live-code docstrings citing never-public names, (b) the absence of any directory map or docs index, and (c) private-only paths on public remotes — a smaller, more mechanical problem than "the mental model's sources are wrong", and arguably a symptom of ranks 1-4 rather than an independent root cause.

disagreements_with_proposals: A (and B, C): `_acquire_daemon_lock_with_timeout` is not a duplicate. daemon/_life_worker_admission.py:64-75 is a 6-line lazy proxy that imports the implementation from daemon/handoff.py:218 (`... as _acquire_daemon_lock_with_timeout_impl` at :33) so `monkeypatch.setattr(life_worker, 'acquire_global_daemon_lock', ...)` keeps working (comment at :52-56). A's instruction 'keep the admission copy, import it in handoff.py' is backwards and would delete the only implementation; B's 'second definition' and C's 'duplicate' deletions would remove a documented test seam.

A: 'tools/subagent/_direct_run.py does NOT import run_contract (it mirrors one path constant at :189)' — false. _direct_run.py:212 `from ...skills import run_contract as rc` and :237 uses rc.DEFAULT_RUN_CONTRACT_PATH. final_plan.verified_diagnosis: Argus feels unclear for one structural reason and several amplifiers, and the verification narrowed each of them. (1) No declared or enforced package order (MOSTLY CONFIRMED): argus_skill/ (687 files, 218,619 LOC, 27 subpackages) has 1,553-1,594 cross-package import statements, 67% inside function bodies; the lazy style is specific to framework seams (79-81% in life/apps/manager/core versus 5.7% for stdlib imports). 33-35 mutual package pairs exist; only 10 of the 1,071 lazy imports are individually necessary cycle-breakers, yet module-level edges alone already make 16 packages one strongly-connected component, so lazy imports hide the mesh rather than hold it together. 181 statements across 53 directed pairs import `_private` modules/names cross-package. `core` has fan-in ~790-798 and exactly 7 module-level outward statements in 5 files (knobs.py:21 and backend_readiness.py:12-13 -> agent_cli; usage.py:22 -> provider_integrations; operator_messages.py:8 and mission_view/_reduce_mission.py:19 -> life; runtime_identity.py:14 -> package root); the diagnosis's claim that core imports manager at module level was CORRECTED (operator_context.py:230 is function-body). Under the 8-layer order recommended here the live tree has exactly 23 module-level upward statements and 66 function-body upward (file, package) pairs (116 statements). About 387 lazily-imported names are monkeypatch targets in tests (documented at daemon/_life_worker_boot.py:6-10, apps/_runtime_construction.py:651-657), so blanket hoisting is unsafe. Eight executable import rules exist across four test files (tests/test_architecture_invariants.py:261/280/300 among 27 passing tests; tests/core/test_vertical_contract.py:356; tests/life/test_result_shortfall_iteration.py:221; tests/proof_ledger/test_proof_ledger_kernel.py:904,931; tests/test_bootstrap_doctor.py:13), but every one guards the vertical seam, proof_ledger or the doctor; none pins core/life/daemon/apps/manager/webapi/tools apart, and docs/architecture-simplification-plan.md:37-45 states intent only for core-vs-vertical. argus_skill/__init__.py:18 eagerly imports loop.SkillLoop, so `import argus_skill.core.paths` loads 71 modules across 8 subpackages (core, engineer, skills, roles, life, reviewer, agent_cli, loop) - not verticals/daemon/apps/webapi. (2) Names (WEAKENED): six 0-byte __init__.py (core 25,804 LOC, apps 11,311, skills 7,595, daemon 6,882, engineer 5,279, adapters 4,292), but 98-100% of modules in them carry docstrings and daemon/engineer/adapters are well named; only core, skills and apps have contents that contradict their names (skills/ is 1,637 LOC of Skill-document code versus 2,533 of vertical/stage machinery and 3,090 of RL-research gates; apps/ holds a 4,621-LOC mission runtime whose own docstring says it is shared by daemon, teammate runner and Manager). webapi's 29/31 FastAPI-free top-level modules are a documented design, but webapi/__init__.py:1 still calls itself the `[web]` extra while pyproject.toml:38,40 make fastapi/uvicorn hard dependencies and no such extra exists. VERTICALS living in skills/vertical_select.py:69-75 is documented deliberate cycle-breaking (verticals/__init__.py:3-14); tools/gpu_lease.py (633) and gpu_ownership.py (541) and skills/rl_training_health.py (526) have zero production importers (gpu_lease is documented as a `python -m` tool in tools/gpu_load.py). (3) The spine (WEAKENED): the chain daemon/_life_worker_run.py:272 -> life/supervisor/_core.py:697/1151 -> _mission_execution_runtime.py:840 -> apps/_runtime_execute.py:412/818 -> loop.py:270 -> engineer/runner.py:103 really crosses five packages plus the root, and its cross-package surface is underscore-named (apps/_runtime.__all__ 19/23 private, life/supervisor/__init__ 24/30, tools/subagent 69/91). But the 13 line-count splits are by lifecycle phase; `_emit_planner_verdict` has ONE implementation (_core.py:1515) plus two `raise NotImplementedError` mixin stubs; the front door is a five-layer composition around one classifier (life/router.py:367); the two LifeSupervisorConfig builders have different signatures and a documented cockpit-vs-daemon duality; `_acquire_daemon_lock_with_timeout` at _life_worker_admission.py:64 is a documented monkeypatch proxy for the implementation at handoff.py:218; LifeSupervisor has 10 mixins / 17 MRO classes / 207-212 methods (not 248). Production consumers of apps/_runtime privates are 4 names in daemon and team; 172-269 test files import private paths. final_plan.recommendation_summary: Adopt Proposal A's shape (name it, pin it, then move the minimum) with the judges' grafts and factual fixes. Day 1 lands, with zero code moves and zero operator decisions, a docs/LAYOUT.md map, docstrings for the six empty packages and the eight stale ones, a PEP 562 lazy root __init__, and a new section of tests/test_architecture_invariants.py that encodes an 8-layer order (kernel, providers, capabilities, domain, roles, runtime, process, delivery) as strict-equality allowlists generated from today's tree (23 module-level upward statements, 66 function-body upward file/package pairs, 53 private-import pairs), plus guards that the cited `python -m` paths in prompts/skills and the argv-matched re-entry modules stay importable and that the Manager-only stage-writer count can only fall. Then eight one-day mechanical batches, each a content-free `git mv` commit followed by one-line import edits with sys.modules alias shims (so monkeypatched names keep resolving): make core a module-level leaf by pulling five stdlib/core-only leaf modules down (backend names, process control, event log, mission outcome, capability vault) and pushing agent_probe out; put ChecklistItem in the contract, the vertical inventory beside the verticals, and the RL gates in verticals/research (re-exported through research_bridge because tools/subagent/_direct_run.py:212 needs run_contract); move the stage machine and vertical selection into pipeline/; move apps/_inbox and _life_actions into life/; give the mission runtime one package (mission_runner/) and make its four cross-package names public; rename cli/->terminal/ and maintenance/->doctor/ and delete all shims in one sed morning; make the vertical loader public (verticals/loader.py etc.). Behaviour-adjacent work (the MemoryBundle.root host-root leak, consolidating ~12 near-identical atomic writes, one ROLES source, dead-module deletion) is confined to two late, test-gated phases behind operator cards, and the test tree is re-filed last. This beats B and C (95k-120k LOC moved, self-contradictory orders, console-script retargets that require `pip install -e` in pinned venvs, behaviour changes hidden in move phases) and D (hand-classified renames of ~1,000 `project_root` sites and wire/event/HTTP renames on the hottest frontend paths) because every step here is rename-detectable, lands within a day against daily concurrent pushes, keeps the suite and the daemons green, adds no runtime mechanism, and leaves an executable, shrinking record of exactly what remains.

operator_decision_cards.question: Confirm the 8-layer order as the intended architecture (kernel < providers < capabilities < domain < [pipeline] < roles < runtime(life, manager, mission_runner) < process(daemon, team) < delivery), in particular: tools BELOW verticals (verticals import image_api etc.), skills (Skill library) below roles, and life + manager + mission_runner as one runtime layer with intra-layer cycles tolerated and counted?
options: Approve as written (23 module-level violations today, 6 after ph7)
Move tools above process (tools/team.py, tools/manager_live_view.py, tools/subagent/_direct_run.py import team/manager/daemon) - then verticals->tools becomes upward (28 statements)
Merge process into runtime (removes daemon->life/manager counting but hides the process boundary)
operator_decision_cards.recommended: Approve as written; the three tools upward edges are pinned with fix notes (their bodies are operator CLIs or process helpers that can move later).
operator_decision_cards.why: It is the order with the fewest module-level violations that also matches docs/PRINCIPLES.md section 2 and every package's own docstring; because the table is data in the test, changing it later is a one-file edit plus a regenerated allowlist.

risks.risk: Rebase conflicts with the paper, Atlas and copilot-quota sessions on hot files: verticals/research/stages.py (125 commits/30d), core/knobs.py (29), life/memory.py (30), apps/_runtime_execute.py (27), skills/vertical_select.py (15), life/supervisor (348 file-touches/30d), webapi (161), manager (181).
risks.mitigation: Every move is a separate content-free `git mv` commit (100% similarity, so rebase re-applies the other side's edits to the new path) followed by a small import-edit commit; hot files change by one import line; each phase is fetched, executed, tested and pushed inside one morning; the ph6 re-point is a re-runnable script; move days are announced the evening before in the handoff doc.

risks.risk: Processes running from a tree whose files change under them lazily import a moved module: the four dev-tree processes (trial.egress, three `--web --no-daemon` servers from /data/v-boxiuli/Argus/.venv) and argus-runtime-latest between fast-forward and restart; after ph6 the shims are gone.
risks.mitigation: Alias shims land in the same commit as every move (ph1-ph5, ph7); each move phase's checklist restarts the dev-tree processes (or moves them to a pinned checkout); the deploy rule is already kill -> checkout -> restart (handoff doc :166); pinned checkouts (daemons on 385d9b33) are separate working trees and are unaffected until they are fast-forwarded.

risks.risk: sys.modules alias shims surprise tooling: objects report __module__ = the new path; a test asserting an old dotted path string would fail; pickling by module path changes.
risks.mitigation: Verified: daemon/config.py and handoff.py persist no dotted module paths; only 1-2 test files patch the shimmed modules by string and they resolve to the same object; shims live at most two phases; the full suite is the gate.

risks.risk: Strict-equality allowlists cause friction for other sessions (a fixed edge left in the list fails; two PRs shrinking the same list conflict).
risks.mitigation: Failure messages print the exact line to delete; lists are sorted one entry per line; edits are one-word deletions; the friction is the ratchet working and is far cheaper than the 27 lazy-only cycles it stops from growing.

risks.risk: Moving cited or argv-matched module paths breaks an Engineer's `python -m` instruction or a daemon's process match mid-campaign (tools.subagent runs live jobs right now; teammate_entry is matched in argv at daemon/state.py:1306).
risks.mitigation: test_module_paths_cited_by_prompts_and_skills_resolve and test_subprocess_reentry_module_paths_stay_importable land in ph0 before any move; tools/* public paths are frozen with permanent forwarders; no plan phase moves team/ or tools/subagent/.

risks.risk: core grows by ~2.1k LOC (backend_names, process_control, event_log, mission_outcome, capability_vault) while PRINCIPLES says 'small stable kernel', and a reviewer reads it as the wrong direction.
risks.mitigation: All five are stdlib-only or core-only leaf modules; the goal is to make core a module-level leaf FIRST so the later ledger/config extraction (card 12) changes only import targets, never directions; core/__init__.py names the tiers and the extraction candidates.

risks.risk: The frozen argus-core binary or its smoke scripts break: desktop-tauri/argus_backend.spec:10-11 and tests/desktop/test_frozen_runtime.py:20-21 import skills.vertical_select.VERTICALS and verticals._base; smoke-trial-release.py:210 cites core.agent_probe.

risks.risk: The MemoryBundle.root fix (ph8) relocates live campaign files (letters.json, RESEARCH_PLAN.md, stage-certificates.json) from the host root into projects/<id>/ while daemons are running.

risks.risk: Scope creep: dedupe or vocabulary work slips into a move phase and changes behaviour under the banner of 'moving'.
risks.mitigation: Behaviour-adjacent work is confined to ph8 and ph9, each behind an operator card, with named tests and a live-project replay check; every other phase's diff is git mv + import lines + shims + tests.

final_plan.estimated_total_churn: Moved content-free by git mv: 44 source files, ~14.5k LOC (core +2,067; verticals/research +3,001; pipeline 2,533; life +693; mission_runner ~5,468; terminal 857; doctor 2,159; adapters +183) plus ~60 test files re-filed in ph10 - history preserved, rename-detectable. Edited: ~450 import lines across ~200 production files and ~240 test files (one line each; the bulk in the ph6 scripted sed), ~120 LOC of real code edits (ChecklistItem/inventory extraction, BackendName rename, version/sandbox/runtime_identity one-liners, public aliases for six runner names, core/paths new names, global_root_or_404 rename), ~90 lines at the 86 MemoryBundle.root sites (ph8, gated), ~250 LOC touched by the atomic-write/ROLES/EVENT_FILE consolidation (ph9, gated). Added: ~450 LOC of tests (section 6 of tests/test_architecture_invariants.py plus the ph2/ph6/ph8/ph9/ph10 tests), ~350 LOC of docs and docstrings (LAYOUT.md, README section, glossary, 14 package docstrings), ~28 five-line shims that all die in ph6/ph10, one core atomic-write function (~40 LOC). Deleted: ~28 shims, tools/subagent/_core.py (124), tools/gpu_ownership.py (541, if approved), ~12 atomic-write copies (~250), five role tuples, two EVENT_FILE constants, three _resolve_global_root copies, MemoryBundle.root and four guessing shims, ~30 LOC of stale docstrings, two tracked npm logs. Zero new runtime mechanisms; zero console-script changes; zero on-disk format changes outside the gated ph8 carry. Eleven landing days (ph0-ph10) spread over roughly four weeks; ph0 needs no restart, ph1-ph9 use the existing kill -> checkout -> restart rule, ph10 is tests plus shim removal. Measurable end state: module-level upward edges 23 -> 6; function-body upward (file, package) pairs 66 -> ~30; private cross-package import pairs 53 -> <30; core module-level outward statements 7 -> 1; verticals -> orchestration imports 30 -> 4 (all lazy, pinned); packages with empty docstrings 6 -> 0; skills/ 7,595 -> ~1,700 LOC; apps/ 11,311 -> ~6,000 LOC; `import argus_skill.core.paths` loads 0 engine modules; atomic_write definitions 19 -> <= 6; role tuples 6 -> 1.
